+# --- advisory voices (D-7.4): after the counted voices, concurrently, one wall clock, findings only under advisory_voices[] ---
+_ADV_ADVISORY_PIDS=""   # "pid=token" pairs of the live advisory walkers (the reapers kill only the process forked)
+_adv_reap_advisory() {
+  local e p
+  for e in ${_ADV_ADVISORY_PIDS:-}; do
+    p="${e%%=*}"
+    [[ "$p" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
+    _adv_is_same "$p" "$e" && { _adv_kill_tree "$p" KILL >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; }
+  done
+  _ADV_ADVISORY_PIDS=""
+  return 0
+}
+_adv_advisory_walk() {  # <voice dir> <type> <sprint id> <timeout> <diff files> <alias> — one advisory voice: the hop, then
+  # process_findings (the same schema, qualification and KF-004 repair rules as a counted voice); its rejected payloads never
+  # land beside the envelope (verdict-derive counts those), and the result is published whole
+  local d="$1" type="$2" sprint_id="$3" timeout="$4" diff_files="$5" alias="$6" raw="" rc=0 res="" st=""
+  export LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REJECT_SIDECAR_DISABLE=1
+  export _ADV_SIDECAR_TAG="advisory"
+  raw=$(_adv_invoke_hop "$alias" "$d/system-prompt.txt" "$d/user-prompt.txt" "$alias" "$timeout" "$d/vq-advisory.json" "$type" "$SCRIPT_DIR/../schemas/wire/dissent-${type}.wire.json") || rc=$?
+  printf '%s' "$rc" > "$d/rc"
+  res=$(process_findings "$raw" "$type" "$alias" "$sprint_id" "$rc" "$diff_files") || res=""
+  if [[ -n "$res" ]]; then st=$(_extract_result_status "$res") || st=""; fi
+  [[ -n "$st" ]] || st="malformed_response"
+  printf '%s' "$res" > "$d/result.json.tmp" && mv -f "$d/result.json.tmp" "$d/result.json"
+  printf '%s' "$st" > "$d/status"
+}
+_adv_run_advisory_voices() {  # <type> <sprint id> <timeout> <diff files> <alias>... — every voice started at once under
+  # $CONF_ADVISORY_TIMEOUT seconds of wall clock for all of them; a voice still running then is killed and marked timed_out.
+  # Each voice's files are under $_ADVERSARIAL_WORKDIR/advisory/<n>/
+  local type="$1" sprint_id="$2" timeout="$3" diff_files="$4"; shift 4
+  local root="$_ADVERSARIAL_WORKDIR/advisory" n=0 a d pid tok e deadline alive
+  mkdir -p "$root" 2>/dev/null || return 1
+  for a in "$@"; do
+    n=$((n + 1)); d="$root/$n"
+    mkdir -p "$d" 2>/dev/null || continue
+    printf '%s' "$a" > "$d/alias"
+    if cp -f "$_ADVERSARIAL_WORKDIR/system-prompt.txt" "$_ADVERSARIAL_WORKDIR/user-prompt.txt" "$d/" 2>/dev/null; then
+      ( _adv_advisory_walk "$d" "$type" "$sprint_id" "$timeout" "$diff_files" "$a" ) >"$d/log" 2>&1 &
+      pid=$!
+      tok=$(_adv_fork_token "$pid") || tok=""
+      _ADV_ADVISORY_PIDS+="${pid}=$(_adv_tok_word "$tok") "
+      printf '%s' "$pid" > "$d/pid"
+    else
+      printf 'prompt_copy_failed' > "$d/status"
+    fi
+  done
+  deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + CONF_ADVISORY_TIMEOUT ))
+  while :; do
+    alive=0
+    for e in $_ADV_ADVISORY_PIDS; do _adv_is_same "${e%%=*}" "$e" && { alive=1; break; }; done
+    (( alive )) || break
+    (( $(date +%s) < deadline )) || break
+    sleep 0.2
+  done
+  for (( a = 1; a <= n; a++ )); do
+    d="$root/$a"; [[ -s "$d/pid" ]] || continue
+    pid=$(cat "$d/pid" 2>/dev/null || true)
+    for e in $_ADV_ADVISORY_PIDS; do
+      [[ "${e%%=*}" == "$pid" ]] || continue
+      if _adv_is_same "$pid" "$e"; then
+        : > "$d/timed_out"
+        _adv_kill_tree "$pid" KILL >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+        log "Advisory voice $(cat "$d/alias"): still running at the ${CONF_ADVISORY_TIMEOUT}s advisory wall clock — killed (timed_out)"
+      fi
+      wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
+    done
+  done
+  _ADV_ADVISORY_PIDS=""
+  return 0
+}
+_adv_advisory_block() {  # <type> <counted result json file> <diff file> <alias>…(planned, in order) — the advisory_voices[]
+  # array on stdout: each planned voice's findings (hallucination-filtered, tagged voice: advisory, linked by duplicate_of to a

+  local type="$1" counted="$2" diff_file="$3"; shift 3

+  local root="${_ADVERSARIAL_WORKDIR:-}/advisory" _av_n=0 _av_alias d st res entry _av_rc _av_err

+      res=$(cat "$d/result.json")
+      case "$(cat "$d/status" 2>/dev/null || echo malformed_response)" in
+        malformed_response|api_failure) st="failed"; _av_err=$(jq -r '.metadata.error // .metadata.status // ""' <<<"$res" | LC_ALL=C tr -d '\000-\037\177' | cut -c1-200) ;;
+        *) st="succeeded"; res=$(_apply_hallucination_filter "$res" "$diff_file") ;;
+      esac
+    elif [[ "$(cat "$d/status" 2>/dev/null || true)" == "prompt_copy_failed" ]]; then st="failed"; _av_err="prompt_copy_failed"
+    else st="failed"; _av_err="the voice left no result"

+      def file: anc | split(":")[0];
+      def lines: ([anc | capture(":(?<a>[0-9]+)(-(?<b>[0-9]+))?$")] | .[0]) as $m
+        | if $m == null then null else ([($m.a | tonumber), (($m.b // $m.a) | tonumber)] | sort) end;
+      def overlaps($x; $y): if $x != null and $y != null then ($x[0] <= $y[1] and $y[0] <= $x[1]) else false end;
+      ($cf[0].findings // []) as $top
+      | ($af[0]) as $r
+      | (if $st == "succeeded" then ($r.findings // []) else [] end) as $fs
+      | {alias: $a, status: $st, counted_as: "advisory_voice",
+         findings: ($fs | to_entries | map(.value as $f
+           | ($f | file) as $ff | ($f | lines) as $fl | ($f | anc) as $fa
+           | ($top | map(select((file) == $ff and $ff != "" and ((.category // "") == ($f.category // ""))
+                                and (if (lines) != null and $fl != null then overlaps(lines; $fl) else (anc) == $fa end)))
+                   | (.[0].id // null)) as $dup
+           | $f + {id: ("DISS-A" + ($n | tostring) + "-" + ((.key + 1) | tostring | if length < 3 then ("000" + .)[-3:] else . end)),
+                   voice: "advisory", answered_by: $a, duplicate_of: $dup})),
+         rejected_count: ($r.metadata.rejected_count // 0), repaired_count: ($r.metadata.repaired_count // 0),
+         rejected_summary: ($r.metadata.rejected_summary // []),
+         cost_usd: ($r.metadata.cost_usd // 0), exit_code: $rc}
+        + (if $err == "" then {} else {error: $err} end)' 2>/dev/null) \
+      || entry=$(jq -cn --arg a "$_av_alias" '{alias: $a, status: "failed", counted_as: "advisory_voice", findings: [], error: "the advisory block could not be built"}')
+    printf '%s\n' "$entry" >> "$blk"
+    log "Advisory voice $_av_alias: $st ($(jq -r '.findings | length' <<<"$entry") finding(s), never counted)"
+  done
+  # the aliases refused by locality, named in the block too (never run)
+  local r_role _av_alias_r _av_prov_r
+  while IFS=$'\t' read -r r_role _av_alias_r _av_prov_r; do
+    [[ "$r_role" == "advisory" && -n "$_av_alias_r" ]] || continue
+    jq -cn --arg a "$_av_alias_r" --arg p "$_av_prov_r" '{alias: $a, status: "refused", counted_as: "advisory_voice", findings: [],
+      error: ("locality: local_voices refuses hosted hop " + $a + " (" + $p + ")")}' >> "$blk"
+  done <<<"$_ADV_LOC_REFUSED"
+  jq -cs '.' "$blk"
+}

  local system_prompt_file="$1"

  # cycle-109 Sprint 2 T2.5 — optional sidecar path. When provided,

  # so the verdict_quality envelope lands in this file. Backward-compat:
  # callers that don't pass the arg get the legacy non-sidecar behavior.
  local vq_sidecar="${5:-}"
  # Cycle-112 D-6 (#931) — attribution type so MODELINV envelopes record
  # which phase of adversarial review (review/audit/design) issued the
  # call. Defaults empty for backward-compat with any pre-D-6 caller.
----COMPANION-WALK----
}

# Walk the companion chain (runs in a background subshell). Writes into
# $workdir: companion.result.json, companion.final, companion.rc,
# companion.status, companion.attempts (one per line), companion.vq (paths of
# the attempts' verdict-quality sidecars).
_walk_companion_chain() {  # <workdir (companion sub-dir)> <prompt_dir> <type> <sprint_id> <timeout> <diff_files> <model>...
  local workdir="$1" prompt_dir="$2" type="$3" sprint_id="$4" timeout="$5" diff_files="$6"; shift 6
  local m raw rc res status final="" last_status="" last_rc=0
  mkdir -p "$workdir"
  : > "$workdir/companion.attempts"; : > "$workdir/companion.vq"
  export _ADV_SIDECAR_TAG="companion"
  for m in "$@"; do
    rc=0
    local vq="$workdir/vq-companion-${m//[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/_}-$$-$RANDOM.json"
    _adv_put_state "$workdir/companion.current" "$m"   # the hop in flight (sixth run, C-001: the reap path names it)
    # main's deadline follows the phase (fifth run, C-001): `queue` while waiting for the CLI lock, `hop`
    # once it is held (the lock helper writes it), `post` after the model answered
    # (nineteenth run, a2 C-001: an HTTP hop whose catalog chain reaches a CLI binary takes that binary's lock BEFORE its
    # request — it queues too, so main's deadline charges the lock wait to the queue, never to the hop)
    if [[ -n "$(_adv_cli_bin_for "$m")" ]]; then _adv_put_state "$workdir/companion.phase" queue; else _adv_put_state "$workdir/companion.phase" hop; fi
    _adv_put_state "$workdir/companion.hop_started_iso" "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ 2>/dev/null || true)"   # (whole — thirty-ninth run, a4a DISS-C-002; the MODELINV lookup window is this hop, not the companion's lifetime — sixteenth run, a3 C-004)
    command rm -f -- "$workdir/companion.lockwait" "$workdir/companion.hop_ended_iso" 2>/dev/null   # (twenty-first run, a3 DISS-C-001: a hop starts with no end time — the previous hop's would invert the fold's MODELINV window and hide a mid-hop reap)
    raw=$(_ADV_PHASE_FILE="$workdir/companion.phase" _ADV_HOP_START_FILE="$workdir/companion.hop_started_iso" _ADV_LOCK_EXPIRED_FILE="$workdir/companion.lockwait" _adv_invoke_hop "$m" "$prompt_dir/system-prompt.txt" "$prompt_dir/user-prompt.txt" "$m" "$timeout" "$vq" "$type" "$SCRIPT_DIR/../schemas/wire/dissent-${type}.wire.json") || rc=$?
    _adv_put_state "$workdir/companion.hop_ended_iso" "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [[ -s "$vq" ]] && echo "$vq" >> "$workdir/companion.vq"
    _adv_put_state "$workdir/companion.phase" post   # the model answered: validation and repair round-trips get their own budget
    # twentieth run, a2 DISS-C-001: the walker runs as a background job, where errexit is live — a failing post-hop helper is
    # an unusable answer for this hop, never the end of the walk with no record
    res=$(process_findings "$raw" "$type" "$m" "$sprint_id" "$rc" "$diff_files") || res=""
    status=""; [[ -n "$res" ]] && { status=$(_extract_result_status "$res") || status=""; }

    local result="$1"

    if [[ -z "$diff_file" ]] || [[ ! -f "$diff_file" ]]; then

     3	The rule, applied at config load to every HTTP provider in the merged ``hounfour.providers`` view:

     6	  (an insecure endpoint is never resolved through DNS, so there is no rebinding), and the address must be
     7	  loopback (``127.0.0.0/8``, ``::1``) or RFC1918 (``10/8``, ``172.16/12``, ``192.168/16``). Link-local,
     8	  the cloud metadata addresses, unique-local IPv6 and every public range are refused.
     9	* An ``http://`` endpoint is admitted only when its host equals the provider's opt-in host. A mismatched
    10	  host, a public ``http`` host or an ``http`` endpoint without an opt-in fails at load with a named reason.
    11	* Every other endpoint keeps the cycle-099 refusals: ``https`` only, no userinfo, no control bytes or path
    12	  traversal, and no loopback, private, link-local, metadata or otherwise blocked IP literal (``localhost``
    13	  included). One provider's opt-in never changes another provider's checks.
    14	* ``keyless: true`` marks a provider that needs no credential; a literal ``auth: "local"`` is accepted and
    15	  normalised to ``keyless: true`` in the merged view. A keyless provider is admitted only when every model
    16	  declares ``context_window`` and ``dispatch_group``.

    21	opt-in and ``validate_declared_endpoint`` (the full pipeline minus the host allowlist, which an

     4	
     5	* ``allow_insecure_endpoint`` is a host STRING, never a boolean. It must be an IP literal or ``localhost``
     6	  (an insecure endpoint is never resolved through DNS, so there is no rebinding), and the address must be
     7	  loopback (``127.0.0.0/8``, ``::1``) or RFC1918 (``10/8``, ``172.16/12``, ``192.168/16``). Link-local,
     8	  the cloud metadata addresses, unique-local IPv6 and every public range are refused.
     9	* An ``http://`` endpoint is admitted only when its host equals the provider's opt-in host. A mismatched
    10	  host, a public ``http`` host or an ``http`` endpoint without an opt-in fails at load with a named reason.
    11	* Every other endpoint keeps the cycle-099 refusals: ``https`` only, no userinfo, no control bytes or path
    12	  traversal, and no loopback, private, link-local, metadata or otherwise blocked IP literal (``localhost``
    13	  included). One provider's opt-in never changes another provider's checks.
    14	* ``keyless: true`` marks a provider that needs no credential; a literal ``auth: "local"`` is accepted and
    15	  normalised to ``keyless: true`` in the merged view. A keyless provider is admitted only when every model
    16	  declares ``context_window`` and ``dispatch_group``.

    21	opt-in and ``validate_declared_endpoint`` (the full pipeline minus the host allowlist, which an

+# llama.cpp `reasoning_content`; some servers `reasoning`). Progress, never content.
+REASONING_DELTA_KEYS = ("reasoning_content", "reasoning")
+
+_LEADING_THINK_BLOCK = re.compile(r"\A\s*<think>(.*?)</think>\s*", re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)
+_LEADING_THINK_OPEN = re.compile(r"\A\s*<think>", re.IGNORECASE)
+
+
+def strip_thinking_blocks(content: str) -> Tuple[str, str, bool]:
+    """Remove the reasoning a model prefixed to its answer: every leading
+    `<think>…</think>` block, and an unterminated leading `<think>` (the rest of the
+    content is then reasoning). Returns (content, removed_thinking, stripped).
+
+    Only LEADING blocks are removed: a `<think>` string inside the answer itself
+    (a finding that quotes a template, say) is content and stays."""
+    if not content:
+        return content, "", False
+    removed: List[str] = []
+    rest = content
+    while True:
+        m = _LEADING_THINK_BLOCK.match(rest)
+        if not m:
+            break
+        removed.append(m.group(1).strip())
+        rest = rest[m.end():]
+    if _LEADING_THINK_OPEN.match(rest):
+        removed.append(_LEADING_THINK_OPEN.sub("", rest, count=1).strip())
+        rest = ""
+    if not removed:
+        return content, "", False
+    return rest, "\n".join(p for p in removed if p), True

+def strip_thinking_blocks(content: str) -> Tuple[str, str, bool]:
+    """Remove the reasoning a model prefixed to its answer: every leading
+    `<think>…</think>` block, and an unterminated leading `<think>` (the rest of the
+    content is then reasoning). Returns (content, removed_thinking, stripped).
+
+    Only LEADING blocks are removed: a `<think>` string inside the answer itself
+    (a finding that quotes a template, say) is content and stays."""
+    if not content:
+        return content, "", False
+    removed: List[str] = []
+    rest = content
+    while True:
+        m = _LEADING_THINK_BLOCK.match(rest)
+        if not m:

+        removed.append(m.group(1).strip())
+        rest = rest[m.end():]
+    if _LEADING_THINK_OPEN.match(rest):
+        removed.append(_LEADING_THINK_OPEN.sub("", rest, count=1).strip())
+        rest = ""
+    if not removed:
+        return content, "", False
+    return rest, "\n".join(p for p in removed if p), True
+

# Fire BB with NO --pr: it self-discovers open PRs and dedups internally.
# BB's stdout (its run JSON) is kept in the handoff dir and replayed, so a DEGRADED run can name its voices.
BB_OUT="${HANDOFF_DIR}/bb-stdout.json"
rc=0
if [[ -x "$BB_ENTRY" ]]; then
    "$BB_ENTRY" --repo "$repo" >"$BB_OUT" || rc=$?
else

cat "$BB_OUT"

# cycle-129 D-7.7 (DEC-0150): exit 3 = the review COMPLETED with a DEGRADED consensus (bridgebuilder.exit_on_degraded;
# 0 restores the old exit). Not a failure: one WARN naming the incomplete voices, `degraded: true` in the handoff, exit 0.
# Bridgebuilder PR #1282 F-001: exit 3 is "completed, degraded" ONLY when the run JSON is there to prove it — a
# non-empty stdout that parses with a `verdicts` array. An exit 3 with no run JSON (a wrapper, a shell error inside
# entry.sh, a reassigned exit code) stays a failure: the handoff records it and the dispatcher exits 3.
degraded=false
voices_json="[]"
if [[ "$rc" -eq 3 ]]; then
    if [[ -s "$BB_OUT" ]] && jq -e '.verdicts | type == "array"' "$BB_OUT" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        degraded=true
        voices_json=$(jq -c '[.verdicts[]?.voices.incomplete[]? | strings] | unique' "$BB_OUT" 2>/dev/null) || voices_json="[]"
        voices=$(jq -r 'join(", ")' <<<"$voices_json" 2>/dev/null) || voices=""
        echo "dispatcher: WARN: bridgebuilder completed DEGRADED (exit 3): incomplete voices: ${voices:-none named (degraded verdict quality)}" >&2
    else
        echo "dispatcher: ERROR: bridgebuilder exited 3 without a run JSON (no verdicts array on stdout) — not a completed review; treated as a failure" >&2
    fi
fi

write_out "$(jq -nc --arg cid "$cycle_id" --arg sid "$schedule_id" \
    --arg repo "$repo" --argjson ec "$rc" --argjson degraded "$degraded" --argjson voices "$voices_json" \
    '{cycle_id:$cid, schedule_id:$sid, dispatched:true, repo:$repo,
      bb_exit_code:$ec, degraded:$degraded}
     + (if $degraded then {incomplete_voices: $voices} else {} end)')"
if [[ "$rc" -eq 3 && "$degraded" == true ]]; then
    exit 0
fi
exit "$rc"

+THE LOCAL-HOP RULE (D-8.1, review round r257-1): a hop is ``local`` only when its provider is an HTTP provider
+(not ``kind: cli`` / ``*-headless``) whose endpoint host is an IP literal in a loopback (``127.0.0.0/8``, ``::1``)
+or RFC1918 (``10/8``, ``172.16/12``, ``192.168/16``) range, or the literal ``localhost`` — exactly the host
+acceptance of the validator's ``check_insecure_optin`` (``local_host`` / ``local_endpoint_host`` below). A
+``dispatch_group: local`` on a model entry or the provider block of any other provider is refused at load; an
+``https`` endpoint on such a host needs no ``allow_insecure_endpoint`` (an ``http`` one still does). The same rule
+is applied at request time (``TransportPolicy.local``), in the planner (``.claude/scripts/lib/hop-locality.py``,
+stdlib mirror) and in Bridgebuilder (``config.ts`` ``localEndpointHost``, TypeScript mirror).
+

+pass the local-hop rule.

+# --- the local-hop rule (D-8.1, r257-1) -------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+LOCAL_RULE_TEXT = "a loopback or RFC1918 IP literal or localhost"
+
+
+def local_host(host: Any) -> Optional[str]:
+    """The canonical host when ``host`` passes the local-hop rule, else None. ONE implementation: the
+    validator's ``check_insecure_optin`` host acceptance (brackets stripped, IP literals canonicalised)."""
+    if not isinstance(host, str) or not host.strip():
+        return None
+    ok, _code, _detail, canonical = _validator().check_insecure_optin(host)
+    return canonical if ok else None
+
+
+def endpoint_host(endpoint: Any) -> str:
+    """The endpoint's canonical host for a refusal message ('' when absent; the raw text when it does not parse)."""
+    if not isinstance(endpoint, str) or not endpoint:
+        return ""
+    try:
+        return split_url(endpoint)[1]
+    except ValueError:
+        return endpoint[:128]
+
+
+def local_endpoint_host(endpoint: Any) -> Optional[str]:
+    """The canonical host when ``endpoint`` is an http(s) URL whose host passes the local-hop rule, else None."""
+    if not isinstance(endpoint, str) or not endpoint:
+        return None
+    try:
+        scheme, host, _port, _path = split_url(endpoint)
+    except ValueError:
+        return None
+    if scheme not in ("http", "https"):
+        return None
+    return local_host(host)
+

# Beads Workflow (beads_rust) — reviewing-code

Referenced from `reviewing-code/SKILL.md` `<beads_workflow>`.

When beads_rust (`br`) is installed, use it to record review feedback:

### Session Start
```bash
# Import latest state from JSONL
br sync --import-only
```

### Recording Review Feedback
```bash
# Add review comment to task
br comments add <task-id> "REVIEW: [verdict] - grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/engineer-feedback.md"

# Mark task status based on review outcome — exactly one of:
# If approved
br label add <task-id> review-approved
# If changes required
br label add <task-id> needs-revision
```
A re-review or re-audit adds its round's label and `br label add` never removes the other, so a task can carry both: the latest `REVIEW:` comment is the verdict of record (with the feedback file and t

### Using Labels for Status
| Label | Meaning | When to Apply |
|-------|---------|---------------|
| `needs-review` | Awaiting review | Before review |
| `review-approved` | Passed review | After "All good" |
| `needs-revision` | Changes requested | After feedback |

### Session End
```bash
# Export SQLite → JSONL before commit
br sync --flush-only
```

### Agent Teams
A teammate runs no `br` command: it reports the result to the lead via SendMessage, and the lead runs it. A comment carries the verdict and the feedback file's path only — never finding text or code

```bash
br label add <task-id> needs-revision
```
A re-review or re-audit adds its round's label and `br label add` never removes the other, so a task can carry both: the latest `REVIEW:` comment is the verdict of record (with the feedback file and t

### Using Labels for Status
| Label | Meaning | When to Apply |
|-------|---------|---------------|
| `needs-review` | Awaiting review | Before review |
| `review-approved` | Passed review | After "All good" |
| `needs-revision` | Changes requested | After feedback |

### Session End
```bash
# Export SQLite → JSONL before commit
br sync --flush-only
```

### Agent Teams
A teammate runs no `br` command: it reports the result to the lead via SendMessage, and the lead runs it. A comment carries the verdict and the feedback file's path only — never finding text or code

# Reviewer concerns — sprint-1 (PR: sprint-257, cycle-129 FR-7 / FR-8)

Scope: pr/head.diff (80 files, 6583 insertions). Cite as head/<path>:<line>.

## Concerns found by the primary reviewer

1. Locality is a label, not a property. `hop-locality.py` (classify, lines 116-134), `modelinv.hop_locality_of` (476),
   `openai_adapter._transport_policy` (221) and Bridgebuilder `isLocalVoice` (config.ts 726-733) call a hop `local`
   whenever its model entry or provider block says `dispatch_group: local`. Nothing checks that the provider's endpoint
   host is loopback/RFC1918/localhost or that the provider is not a CLI hop. Reproduced: a declared provider with
   endpoint https://api.together.xyz/v1 and `dispatch_group: local` classifies `local`; under `hounfour.locality:
   local_voices` the dissent, Flatline and Bridgebuilder would dispatch to it.
2. Bridgebuilder trusted config only governs Bridgebuilder's own plan; every voice dispatches through cheval, which
   reads the CHECKOUT's `.loa.config.yaml`. On a PR-head checkout the head can change a trusted provider's endpoint
   (or aliases) and cheval sends the prompt and the `{env:VAR}` credential there. SKILL.md 117-118 claims the keys
   "follow the trusted-source precedence even when the checkout is a PR head".
3. dispatcher.sh 78-90: exit 3 is treated as completed-degraded and converted to exit 0 without checking that the run
   JSON (a `verdicts` array) exists on stdout.
4. model-health-probe.sh 1469-1475: `_probe_configured` validates with the probe allowlist, so a configured https
   provider on a non-allowlisted host (Example 3, Azure) is "endpoint refused" while cheval admits it.
5. Budget gate now sums primary + companion first hop + advisory voices (adversarial-review.sh 4329-4335) but
   `.loa.config.yaml.example` 1624-1627 still says the companion voice is NOT counted.
6. config.ts 482: any literal `auth` is keyless in Bridgebuilder; cheval normalises only `auth: "local"`.
7. endpoint-validator.py 1047/1054: `localhost` opt-in is admitted with the claim it is "never resolved"; it is
   resolved by the OS resolver when the request is sent.
8. Advisory voices: each hop is still bounded by `timeout_seconds` (60 default); `advisory_timeout_seconds` is only an
   outer bound.
9. README.md 22 links a CHANGELOG entry that this PR does not add.

## Areas the dissenter should probe
- adversarial-review.sh advisory walker / block (3800-4030) — process lifecycle, jq operand sizes, sidecar disable.

- openai_adapter.py — schema-rejection retry heuristic, keyless header omission.

# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (the PR description, `pr/PR.md`)

Scope reviewed: `pr/head.diff` — 80 files, 6583 insertions / 198 deletions; 30 of the files are generated `dist/` output and source maps. Citations are `head/<path>:<line>` with line numbers from `pr/head/`. No PRD/SDD/integration-context exists in this workspace; `grimoires/loa/known-failures.md` is absent (surfaced as a WARN at session start); `br` is not installed, so the beads steps were skipped.

## Overall Assessment

The sprint delivers four things: advisory open-weight voices for the dissent script, the `hounfour.locality: local_voices` posture across the dissent, Flatline, Bridgebuilder and the health probe, Bridgebuilder's trusted-configuration source plus the DEGRADED exit code, and an end-to-end local-hop test. The engineering is careful in the places it looks: every shell operand that reaches `jq`/`yq` is validated or passed as a file, the endpoint opt-in reuses the one canonical validator on both the bash and cheval paths, the TransportPolicy disables proxies and redirects on both the httpx and urllib paths, and the default hosted envelope is left byte-identical (I ran the head validator against the shipped default endpoints, including the templated `bedrock` host — all admit).

Two findings block the merge. First, the `local_voices` posture is satisfied by a label: `dispatch_group: local` on any model or provider block makes a hop "local" with no check that its endpoint is actually a loopback/RFC1918/localhost HTTP endpoint. I reproduced this with the head's own classifier against a declared provider whose endpoint is `https://api.together.xyz/v1`. The config example sells the posture with a threat model ("the prompt does not cross a public network"), and the label does not hold it. Second, Bridgebuilder's trusted configuration only governs Bridgebuilder's planning; every voice still dispatches through cheval, which reads the checkout's `.loa.config.yaml`. The SKILL.md added in this PR claims the trusted precedence holds "even when the checkout is a PR head", which the code does not deliver.

The implementation report (`reviewer.md` = the PR title line) carries no `## AC Verification` walkthrough, no stated assumptions and no record of which self-checks ran; by the skill's rule that alone is an automatic CHANGES_REQUIRED, independent of the findings above.

Six medium and five low observations follow; none of them is counted in the verdict.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

## Changes Required

### 1. Security posture — locality is a declaration, not a property

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/lib/hop-locality.py:116` — under `hounfour.locality: local_voices` a hop is planned as `local` whenever its model entry or provider block says `dispatch_group: local`; the endpoint host is never examined, so a hosted provider labelled `local` is dispatched to and the posture's guarantee does not hold.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/lib/hop-locality.py:116-134` (classify); the same label-only rule in `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/audit/modelinv.py:476` (`hop_locality_of`, the MODELINV record), `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/openai_adapter.py:221` (`_transport_policy`) and `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:726-733` (`isLocalVoice`).
**Issue:** The classifier's rule is "`dispatch_group: local` on the entry or its provider block, and every fallback hop local by the same rule" (`hop-locality.py:11-17`). Reproduced with the head script against the shipped catalog plus this overlay:
```yaml
hounfour:
  locality: local_voices
  providers:
    hosted-oss:
      type: openai_compat
      endpoint: "https://api.together.xyz/v1"
      auth: "{env:LOA_TOGETHER_KEY}"
      models:
        llama-70b: {dispatch_group: local, context_window: 131072}
    openai:
      models:
        gpt-5.5: {dispatch_group: local, fallback_chain: []}
```
```
$ python3 -I hop-locality.py --catalog model-config.yaml --config overlay.yaml -- hosted-oss:llama-70b gpt-5.5
hosted-oss:llama-70b	hosted-oss	local	dispatch_group=local
gpt-5.5	openai	local	dispatch_group=local
```
Both hosted hops are `local`; `adversarial-review.sh` and `flatline-orchestrator.sh` would plan them, Bridgebuilder's `isLocalVoice` keeps them (it does not even consult `fallback_chain`, unlike the Python classifier), cheval's TransportPolicy is applied to a public host, and MODELINV records `hop_locality: local`. A CLI provider block labelled `local` (e.g. `anthropic-headless: {dispatch_group: local}`) is likewise admitted by `isLocalVoice`. Nothing at load time (`endpoint_policy.validate_providers`) refuses the label on a provider that cannot honour it.
**Why This Matters:** `local_voices` is the sprint's confidentiality posture; `.loa.config.yaml.example:1227-1233` describes its threat model as the prompt never crossing a public network. A posture that a single YAML key on any provider defeats, with no refusal and a MODELINV row that says `local`, is worse than no posture: the audit trail asserts something false. The rule is also applied in four places (bash planner, Python telemetry, Python transport, TypeScript planner) with two different definitions (fallback chains considered in one, ignored in another).
**Required Fix:** Define "local" as a property the provider can be checked for: an HTTP provider (not `*-headless`, not `kind: cli`) whose declared endpoint host passes the validator's `check_insecure_optin` host acceptance (loopback, RFC1918 or `localhost`). Refuse `dispatch_group: local` at load (`endpoint_policy.validate_providers`) on any provider that fails it, apply the same rule in `hop_locality_of`, `_transport_policy` (and check the request host at request time), `hop-locality.py` and `isLocalVoice` (including `fallback_chain`, as the Python classifier already does), and add one test per surface with a hosted-endpoint provider labelled `local`. Keep one implementation where the languages allow (cheval + MODELINV + loader share `endpoint_policy`; the bash and TS planners mirror its host rule).
**Reference:** CWE-693 (Protection Mechanism Failure); CWE-807 (Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision); OWASP A05:2021 Security Misconfiguration.

### 2. Security — the trusted configuration never reaches the process that sends the prompt

- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/SKILL.md:117` — on a PR-head checkout Bridgebuilder reads providers/locality/exit from the base branch, but each voice is dispatched by cheval, which loads the checkout's `.loa.config.yaml`; a head that keeps a trusted provider's `keyless`/opt-in flags but changes its `endpoint`, `aliases` or `secret_env_allowlist` is admitted and the prompt (and a `{env:VAR}` credential) go where the head says.
**File:** `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/SKILL.md:117-118` (the claim); `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:602-605` and `:678-700` (`loadTrustedConfig` reads the head only for keyless/insecure declarations the trusted source lacks); `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/core/multi-model-pipeline.ts:220-235` (the voice is created with no key and handed to the cheval delegate).
**Issue:** `headOnlyRefused` compares only two booleans per provider (`keylessOnlyInHead`, `insecureOnlyInHead`). A PR head that leaves `local-vllm: {keyless: true, allow_insecure_endpoint: "127.0.0.1"}` identical to the base but rewrites `endpoint` to `https://attacker.example/v1` (an operator-declared https endpoint skips the host allowlist in `validate_declared_endpoint`, `endpoint-validator.py:1289-1296`), or re-points `hounfour.aliases.<voice>` at a different provider, passes every check here; cheval then loads the checkout config and dispatches the review prompt there. For a trusted provider with `auth: "{env:X}"`, the Bearer credential travels with it. The pre-existing SKILL.md text records this invocation model as "no PR-head checkout" (`:116-117`); the sentence this PR adds (`:117-118`) asserts protection in exactly that case.
**Why This Matters:** The feature's stated purpose (D-7.5) is that an attacker-controlled head cannot declare its way to a credential or an insecure hop. The control is placed in Bridgebuilder's planner while the dispatch path reads a different file; the documentation now promises more than the code holds. Confidence is medium because the shipped scheduled invocation (`dispatcher.sh --repo`) runs in local mode on a trusted checkout; the exposure is the PR-event/`--pr` path the PR documents.
**Required Fix:** Either (a) on a pull request compute drift between the head's and the trusted view's `hounfour.providers`, `hounfour.aliases`, `hounfour.locality` and the secret allowlists and refuse the multi-model run on any difference with a distinct exit code, or (b) hand the trusted configuration to cheval explicitly (a config path cheval loads instead of the checkout's) so the dispatch reads what Bridgebuilder trusted. Correct SKILL.md to state exactly what is protected. Add a test where the head changes only `endpoint` of a trusted keyless provider.
**Reference:** CWE-693 (Protection Mechanism Failure); CWE-829 (Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere); OWASP A08:2021 Software and Data Integrity Failures.

  TITLE: -
  DESC: Rows that previously carried `pricing_source: config` now carry `stale_catalog` for any catalog entry older than 90 days. `rollup.py` was taught the new value, but other readers of the ledger that whitelist `config`/`cli_reported` (cost-report.sh's unpriced/priced split, any dashboards or bats fixtures) will classify these priced rows as unpriced the day a catalog entry crosses the threshold, with no code change on their side. Because the threshold is wall-clock relative, this flips silently in production.
  FAIL: Cost reports start under-counting priced spend and over-counting 'unpriced calls' exactly 90 days after a price_date, with no deploy to correlate it to.
  FIX: Grep every ledger reader for `pricing_source` and add `stale_catalog` to each allow-list in the same PR (cost-report.sh at minimum), or keep `pricing_source: config` and record staleness in a separate additive field (`pricing_stale: true`) so existing consumers are unaffected.

  TITLE: -
  DESC: The schema-rejection heuristic fires on any HTTP 400 whose JSON body contains the substring `response_format` or `json_schema` anywhere. That matches the intended case (server lacks structured-output support) but equally matches (a) a hosted OpenAI 400 saying the operator's own schema is invalid (`Invalid schema for response_format ...`), and (b) a 400 that echoes the prompt back when the prompt itself mentions `json_schema`. # Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (the PR description, `pr/PR.md`)

Scope reviewed: `pr/head.diff` — 80 files, 6583 insertions / 198 deletions; 30 of the files are generated `dist/` output and source maps. Citations are `head/<path>:<line>` with line numbers from `pr/head/`. No PRD/SDD/integration-context exists in this workspace; `grimoires/loa/known-failures.md` is absent (surfaced as a WARN at session start); `br` is not installed, so the beads steps were skipped.

---

## Overall Assessment

The sprint delivers four things: advisory open-weight voices for the dissent script, the `hounfour.locality: local_voices` posture across the dissent, Flatline, Bridgebuilder and the health probe, Bridgebuilder's trusted-configuration source plus the DEGRADED exit code, and an end-to-end local-hop test. The engineering is careful in the places it looks: every shell operand that reaches `jq`/`yq` is validated or passed as a file, the endpoint opt-in reuses the one canonical validator on both the bash and cheval paths, the TransportPolicy disables proxies and redirects on both the httpx and urllib paths, and the default hosted envelope is left byte-identical (I ran the head validator against the shipped default endpoints, including the templated `bedrock` host — all admit).

Two findings block the merge. First, the `local_voices` posture is satisfied by a label: `dispatch_group: local` on any model or provider block makes a hop "local" with no check that its endpoint is actually a loopback/RFC1918/localhost HTTP endpoint. I reproduced this with the head's own classifier against a declared provider whose endpoint is `https://api.together.xyz/v1`. The config example sells the posture with a threat model ("the prompt does not cross a public network"), and the label does not hold it; the dissent's BLOCKING finding adds that the label is not even read consistently — a provider-block label is honoured by the planners but ignored by cheval's transport and MODELINV. Second, Bridgebuilder's trusted configuration only governs Bridgebuilder's planning; every voice still dispatches through cheval, which reads the checkout's `.loa.config.yaml`. The SKILL.md added in this PR claims the trusted precedence holds "even when the checkout is a PR head", which the code does not deliver.

The implementation report (`reviewer.md` = the PR title line) carries no `## AC Verification` walkthrough, no stated assumptions and no record of which self-checks ran; by the skill's rule that alone is an automatic CHANGES_REQUIRED, independent of the findings above.

Seven medium and seven low observations follow; none of them is counted in the verdict.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Security posture — locality is a declaration, not a property

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/lib/hop-locality.py:116` — under `hounfour.locality: local_voices` a hop is planned as `local` whenever its model entry or provider block says `dispatch_group: local`; the endpoint host is never examined, so a hosted provider labelled `local` is dispatched to and the posture's guarantee does not hold.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/lib/hop-locality.py:116-134` (classify); the same label-only rule in `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/audit/modelinv.py:476` (`hop_locality_of`, the MODELINV record), `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/openai_adapter.py:221` (`_transport_policy`) and `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:726-733` (`isLocalVoice`); the label is read from different places at `head/.claude/adapters/cheval.py:541` (model entry only).
**Issue:** The classifier's rule is "`dispatch_group: local` on the entry or its provider block, and every fallback hop local by the same rule" (`hop-locality.py:11-17`). Reproduced with the head script against the shipped catalog plus this overlay:
```yaml
hounfour:
  locality: local_voices
  providers:
    hosted-oss:
      type: openai_compat
      endpoint: "https://api.together.xyz/v1"
      auth: "{env:LOA_TOGETHER_KEY}"
      models:
        llama-70b: {dispatch_group: local, context_window: 131072}
    openai:
      models:
        gpt-5.5: {dispatch_group: local, fallback_chain: []}
```
```
$ python3 -I hop-locality.py --catalog model-config.yaml --config overlay.yaml -- hosted-oss:llama-70b gpt-5.5
hosted-oss:llama-70b	hosted-oss	local	dispatch_group=local
gpt-5.5	openai	local	dispatch_group=local
```
Both hosted hops are `local`; `adversarial-review.sh` and `flatline-orchestrator.sh` would plan them, Bridgebuilder's `isLocalVoice` keeps them (it does not even consult `fallback_chain`, unlike the Python classifier), cheval's TransportPolicy is applied to a public host, and MODELINV records `hop_locality: local`. A CLI provider block labelled `local` (e.g. `anthropic-headless: {dispatch_group: local}`) is likewise admitted by `isLocalVoice`. Nothing at load time (`endpoint_policy.validate_providers`) refuses the label on a provider that cannot honour it.
The dissent (DISS-C-001, confirmed against the head) adds the inverse failure: a label on the PROVIDER block is honoured by `hop-locality.py:116` and `isLocalVoice`, but `_build_provider_config` reads only `model_data.get("dispatch_group")` (`cheval.py:541`), so `_transport_policy` returns None and `hop_locality_of` says `hosted` — a hop planned and admitted as local runs without the D-7.2 request-time rules (proxy env honoured, redirects followed, no path check) and the audit row contradicts the planner.
**Why This Matters:** `local_voices` is the sprint's confidentiality posture; `.loa.config.yaml.example:1227-1233` describes its threat model as the prompt never crossing a public network. A posture that a single YAML key on any provider defeats, with no refusal and a MODELINV row that says `local`, is worse than no posture: the audit trail asserts something false. The rule is applied in four places (bash planner, Python telemetry, Python transport, TypeScript planner) with three different readings (fallback chains considered or not; provider-block label honoured or not).
**Required Fix:** Define "local" as a property the provider can be checked for: an HTTP provider (not `*-headless`, not `kind: cli`) whose declared endpoint host passes the validator's `check_insecure_optin` host acceptance (loopback, RFC1918 or `localhost`). Refuse `dispatch_group: local` at load (`endpoint_policy.validate_providers`) on any provider that fails it; resolve the label once (entry, else provider block) and apply the same rule in `hop_locality_of`, `_transport_policy` (and check the request host at request time), `hop-locality.py` and `isLocalVoice` (including `fallback_chain`, as the Python classifier already does). Add one test per surface with a hosted-endpoint provider labelled `local` and one with a provider-block label. Keep one implementation where the languages allow (cheval + MODELINV + loader share `endpoint_policy`; the bash and TS planners mirror its host rule).
**Reference:** CWE-693 (Protection Mechanism Failure); CWE-807 (Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision); OWASP A05:2021 Security Misconfiguration.

### 2. Security — the trusted configuration never reaches the process that sends the prompt

- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/SKILL.md:117` — on a PR-head checkout Bridgebuilder reads providers/locality/exit from the base branch, but each voice is dispatched by cheval, which loads the checkout's `.loa.config.yaml`; a head that keeps a trusted provider's `keyless`/opt-in flags but changes its `endpoint`, `aliases` or `secret_env_allowlist` is admitted and the prompt (and a `{env:VAR}` credential) go where the head says.
**File:** `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/SKILL.md:117-118` (the claim); `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:602-605` and `:678-700` (`loadTrustedConfig` reads the head only for keyless/insecure declarations the trusted source lacks); `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/core/multi-model-pipeline.ts:220-235` (the voice is created with no key and handed to the cheval delegate).
**Issue:** `headOnlyRefused` compares only two booleans per provider (`keylessOnlyInHead`, `insecureOnlyInHead`). A PR head that leaves `local-vllm: {keyless: true, allow_insecure_endpoint: "127.0.0.1"}` identical to the base but rewrites `endpoint` to `https://attacker.example/v1` (an operator-declared https endpoint skips the host allowlist in `validate_declared_endpoint`, `endpoint-validator.py:1289-1296`), or re-points `hounfour.aliases.<voice>` at a different provider, passes every check here; cheval then loads the checkout config and dispatches the review prompt there. For a trusted provider with `auth: "{env:X}"`, the Bearer credential travels with it. The pre-existing SKILL.md text records this invocation model as "no PR-head checkout" (`:116-117`); the sentence this PR adds (`:117-118`) asserts protection in exactly that case.
**Why This Matters:** The feature's stated purpose (D-7.5) is that an attacker-controlled head cannot declare its way to a credential or an insecure hop. The control is placed in Bridgebuilder's planner while the dispatch path reads a different file; the documentation now promises more than the code holds. Confidence is medium because the shipped scheduled invocation (`dispatcher.sh --repo`) runs in local mode on a trusted checkout; the exposure is the PR-event/`--pr` path the PR documents.
**Required Fix:** Either (a) on a pull request compute drift between the head's and the trusted view's `hounfour.providers`, `hounfour.aliases`, `hounfour.locality` and the secret allowlists and refuse the multi-model run on any difference with a distinct exit code, or (b) hand the trusted configuration to cheval explicitly (a config path cheval loads instead of the checkout's) so the dispatch reads what Bridgebuilder trusted. Correct SKILL.md to state exactly what is protected. Add a test where the head changes only `endpoint` of a trusted keyless provider.
**Reference:** CWE-693 (Protection Mechanism Failure); CWE-829 (Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere); OWASP A08:2021 Software and Data Integrity Failures.

---

## Observations

### 1. Callers — an exit 3 with nothing to show for it becomes success

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/skills/scheduled-cycle-template/contracts/session-cap-bb/dispatcher.sh:78` — `rc == 3` is recorded as `degraded: true` and converted to `exit 0` (`:89-90`) without checking that `bb-stdout.json` holds a run JSON; an exit 3 from any other source (a shell error inside `entry.sh`, a wrapper, a mixed-version `dist/`) is reported as a completed review.
**File:** `head/.claude/skills/scheduled-cycle-template/contracts/session-cap-bb/dispatcher.sh:78-90`
**Suggestion:** Treat 3 as completed-degraded only when `[[ -s "$BB_OUT" ]] && jq -e '.verdicts | type == "array"' "$BB_OUT"`; otherwise log an ERROR and `exit 3`. `_bb_surface_exit` in `spiral-harness.sh:697-711` already tolerates an empty file (it was `|| true` before), so only the dispatcher's exit conversion needs the guard. Add a bats case with exit 3 and empty stdout (none of the four dispatcher cases in `bb-exit-degraded-callers.bats:39-65` covers it).
**Benefit:** The scheduled contract keeps its pre-cycle-129 property that a non-zero Bridgebuilder exit without a review is a failure.

### 2. Health probe — configured https providers are refused by the probe's own allowlist

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/model-health-probe.sh:1469` — `_probe_configured` validates `<endpoint>/models` with `--allowlist "$PROBE_PROVIDERS_ALLOWLIST"` (`:1469-1475`), i.e. the full `validate()` pipeline including step-8 host allowlisting, while the cheval loader admits the same provider through `validate_declared_endpoint` (allowlist skipped). A configured https provider on any host not in `lib/allowlists/loa-providers.json` — Example 3 (`azure-openai`, `.loa.config.yaml.example:1204-1224`) — is reported `UNKNOWN / endpoint_refused` and never probed.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/model-health-probe.sh:1469-1475`
**Suggestion:** Add a `--declared-endpoint` mode to `endpoint-validator.py`/`.sh` that calls `validate_declared_endpoint`, and use it for configured providers (the built-in four keep the allowlist). The header comment at `:852-856` ("apply exactly as on the cheval path") then becomes true. The bats file covers only the 127.0.0.1 opt-in and load-time refusals; add an https non-allowlisted case.
**Benefit:** `--provider <name>` works for the hosted open-weight APIs the PR title advertises, not only loopback servers.

### 3. Budget gate — the example's contract contradicts the code

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.loa.config.yaml.example:1624` — the `budget_cents` comment still says the gate prices "ONE dissent call" and that "the companion voice … are further calls it does not count", while `head/.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh:4329-4335` now sums the primary, the companion's first hop and every advisory voice; the FR-7 paragraph a few lines below (`:1675-1683`) says the opposite of `:1624-1627`.
**File:** `head/.loa.config.yaml.example:1624-1627`; `head/.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh:4320-4341`
**Suggestion:** Rewrite the `budget_cents` comment to the summed contract and state the default-config consequence: with `gpt-5.3-codex` (1.75/14 USD per Mtok in the catalog) and no Anthropic key the companion is `claude-headless` (10/50), so a 150c budget now refuses diffs above ~350 KB where it admitted up to ~430 KB before; with an Anthropic key (`opus`, 4/20) the new estimate is lower than the old fixed rate. Mention this in the CHANGELOG migration notes or raise the shipped default.
**Benefit:** Operators reading the example get the gate's real arithmetic; a mid-size diff that starts exiting 4 after the upgrade is explained.

### 4. Documentation — the CHANGELOG this PR points at is not in this PR

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/README.md:22` — the new README block links a CHANGELOG "Unreleased — earned guards and open voices" entry and `:32` tells users to "see the CHANGELOG Migration notes", but `CHANGELOG.md` is not among the 80 touched files, and this sprint changes caller-visible contracts: Bridgebuilder exit 3 now means DEGRADED and the missing-dependency preflight moved to exit 4 (`head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/SKILL.md:161-162`, `resources/entry.sh:118-120`), `pricing_source: stale_catalog` appears in ledger rows, the dissent budget estimate changed (observation 3), and `http://` provider endpoints without an opt-in now fail config load.
**File:** `head/README.md:22-32`
**Suggestion:** Add the CHANGELOG entry and migration notes in this PR (the skill's documentation check wants one per task), covering the exit-code contract, `exit_on_degraded: 0`, the load-time endpoint rule and the budget arithmetic. If the entry already landed in an earlier sprint of cycle-129, say so in the PR description so a reviewer can verify it.
**Benefit:** The upgrade path this README promises exists where it says it does.

### 5. FAST-GATE: no record of the fast gate in the report

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md:1` — the implementation report is the PR title; it names no formatter check, type check, shellcheck, `pytest` or `bats` run. The rebuilt `dist/` (`head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/dist/.build-manifest.json`) implies `tsc` ran, but nothing shows the six new Python test files, the seven new bats files or the three TypeScript tests passing, and this workspace holds only touched files so I could not run them.
**Suggestion:** Record the self-checks (commands and results) in the report. The tests I read assert the implemented behaviour precisely (ADV-1…9, BUD-1…6, LOC-1…8, FLL-1…7, the probe, dispatcher and trusted-config suites, the local-hop E2E); the gaps are the cases named above (hosted provider labelled local; provider-block label; probe with an https configured provider; dispatcher exit 3 with empty stdout).

### 6. SIMPLICITY[shrink]: three functions well over the 50-line ceiling

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/model-health-probe.sh:1428` — `_probe_configured` runs 118 lines (`:1428-1545`): config read, five early-return classifications, URL validation, auth selection, the curl and a four-way status switch that duplicates `_probe_openai`'s 200/401/403/other handling. `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:605` — `loadTrustedConfig` runs 110 lines (`:605-714`) mixing source selection, parsing, head-refusal, locality and exit-code validation. `head/.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh:3972` — `_adv_advisory_block` runs ~70 lines with a 25-line embedded jq program.

### 7. Transport — `trust_env=False` also drops the operator's CA bundle under httpx

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/base.py:300` — for a policy hop the httpx client is built with `trust_env=False` (also `:397`, `:533`). In httpx that switch disables proxy discovery and `SSL_CERT_FILE`/`SSL_CERT_DIR` alike, while the urllib fallback still honours them through OpenSSL. An https local or opted-in hop presenting a private-CA certificate that the operator trusts via `SSL_CERT_FILE` fails TLS verification on a host with httpx installed and succeeds on one without. (Dissent DISS-C-005, confirmed against the head.)
**Suggestion:** Keep redirects and proxies off but pass an explicit `verify=ssl.create_default_context()` (which loads `SSL_CERT_FILE`/`SSL_CERT_DIR`), or disable proxies via `mounts`/`proxy=None` instead of `trust_env=False`, at the three sites; add a test with a self-signed local https stub.

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:482` — any literal `auth` value without `{env:` is treated as keyless (`literalAuth`), while cheval normalises only the literal `"local"` (`head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/endpoint_policy.py:50`, `:139`) and treats any other literal as a real key. **Suggestion:** Match cheval: keyless iff `keyless: true` or `auth` equals `local` (case-insensitive, trimmed).

### 9. `localhost` opt-in is resolved by the system resolver

- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/scripts/lib/endpoint-validator.py:1047` — `check_insecure_optin` admits `localhost` under the claim that an insecure endpoint "is never resolved, so it cannot be rebound" (`:1054`; repeated at `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/endpoint_policy.py:6`). An IP literal is not resolved; `localhost` is, by the OS resolver (`/etc/hosts`, nsswitch) at request time, and nothing in `TransportPolicy.check_url` (`providers/base.py:131-146`) verifies it resolves to loopback.
**Suggestion:** Either drop `localhost` from the opt-in (IP literals only) or resolve it in `TransportPolicy.check_url` and require every address to be loopback (fail closed on resolver error). Correct the two comments.

### 10. Advisory voices are still cut at the per-call timeout

- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh:3920` — `_adv_advisory_walk` invokes each advisory hop with `$timeout` (`flatline_protocol.<gate>.timeout_seconds`, default 60 at `.loa.config.yaml.example:1623`); `advisory_timeout_seconds` (default 600) is only an outer bound on the group. The use case the example gives — a CPU server with `first_token_deadline_s: 120` (`:1253`) — is killed at 60 s before its own first-token deadline.
**Suggestion:** Either give advisory hops `min(advisory_timeout_seconds, per-hop deadline from the model's streaming_recovery)` or document that `timeout_seconds` still bounds each advisory call.

### 11. SURGICAL: prose trims outside the sprint's scope

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:246` — this PR removes the worked example `("implemented in src/", "done")`, "(nothing after it)" after the trailer rule (`:253`), "(paths only)" (`:211`) and the matching phrases in `auditing-security/SKILL.md` (`:159`, `:238`, `:246`). These are prompt-budget trims unrelated to advisory voices; only the one-line "Read `advisory_voices[].findings` as advisory input" belongs to the sprint.
**Suggestion:** Land budget trims in their own commit with the `check-prompt-budget.sh` result, so the review of this sprint's behaviour is not mixed with edits to the reviewer's own instructions.

# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (the PR description, `pr/PR.md`)

Scope reviewed: `pr/head.diff` — 80 files, 6583 insertions / 198 deletions; 30 of the files are generated `dist/` output and source maps. Citations are `head/<path>:<line>` with line numbers from `pr/head/`. No PRD/SDD/integration-context exists in this workspace; `grimoires/loa/known-failures.md` is absent (surfaced as a WARN at session start); `br` is not installed, so the beads steps were skipped.

---

## Overall Assessment

The sprint delivers four things: advisory open-weight voices for the dissent script, the `hounfour.locality: local_voices` posture across the dissent, Flatline, Bridgebuilder and the health probe, Bridgebuilder's trusted-configuration source plus the DEGRADED exit code, and an end-to-end local-hop test. The engineering is careful in the places it looks: every shell operand that reaches `jq`/`yq` is validated or passed as a file, the endpoint opt-in reuses the one canonical validator on both the bash and cheval paths, the TransportPolicy disables proxies and redirects on both the httpx and urllib paths, and the default hosted envelope is left byte-identical (I ran the head validator against the shipped default endpoints, including the templated `bedrock` host — all admit).

Two findings block the merge. First, the `local_voices` posture is satisfied by a label: `dispatch_group: local` on any model or provider block makes a hop "local" with no check that its endpoint is actually a loopback/RFC1918/localhost HTTP endpoint. I reproduced this with the head's own classifier against a declared provider whose endpoint is `https://api.together.xyz/v1`. The config example sells the posture with a threat model ("the prompt does not cross a public network"), and the label does not hold it. Second, Bridgebuilder's trusted configuration only governs Bridgebuilder's planning; every voice still dispatches through cheval, which reads the checkout's `.loa.config.yaml`. The SKILL.md added in this PR claims the trusted precedence holds "even when the checkout is a PR head", which the code does not deliver.

The implementation report (`reviewer.md` = the PR title line) carries no `## AC Verification` walkthrough, no stated assumptions and no record of which self-checks ran; by the skill's rule that alone is an automatic CHANGES_REQUIRED, independent of the findings above.

Six medium and five low observations follow; none of them is counted in the verdict.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Security posture — locality is a declaration, not a property

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/lib/hop-locality.py:116` — under `hounfour.locality: local_voices` a hop is planned as `local` whenever its model entry or provider block says `dispatch_group: local`; the endpoint host is never examined, so a hosted provider labelled `local` is dispatched to and the posture's guarantee does not hold.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/lib/hop-locality.py:116-134` (classify); the same label-only rule in `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/audit/modelinv.py:476` (`hop_locality_of`, the MODELINV record), `head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/openai_adapter.py:221` (`_transport_policy`) and `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:726-733` (`isLocalVoice`).
**Issue:** The classifier's rule is "`dispatch_group: local` on the entry or its provider block, and every fallback hop local by the same rule" (`hop-locality.py:11-17`). Reproduced with the head script against the shipped catalog plus this overlay:
```yaml
hounfour:
  locality: local_voices
  providers:
    hosted-oss:
      type: openai_compat
      endpoint: "https://api.together.xyz/v1"
      auth: "{env:LOA_TOGETHER_KEY}"
      models:
        llama-70b: {dispatch_group: local, context_window: 131072}
    openai:
      models:
        gpt-5.5: {dispatch_group: local, fallback_chain: []}
```
```
$ python3 -I hop-locality.py --catalog model-config.yaml --config overlay.yaml -- hosted-oss:llama-70b gpt-5.5
hosted-oss:llama-70b	hosted-oss	local	dispatch_group=local
gpt-5.5	openai	local	dispatch_group=local
```
Both hosted hops are `local`; `adversarial-review.sh` and `flatline-orchestrator.sh` would plan them, Bridgebuilder's `isLocalVoice` keeps them (it does not even consult `fallback_chain`, unlike the Python classifier), cheval's TransportPolicy is applied to a public host, and MODELINV records `hop_locality: local`. A CLI provider block labelled `local` (e.g. `anthropic-headless: {dispatch_group: local}`) is likewise admitted by `isLocalVoice`. Nothing at load time (`endpoint_policy.validate_providers`) refuses the label on a provider that cannot honour it.
**Why This Matters:** `local_voices` is the sprint's confidentiality posture; `.loa.config.yaml.example:1227-1233` describes its threat model as the prompt never crossing a public network. A posture that a single YAML key on any provider defeats, with no refusal and a MODELINV row that says `local`, is worse than no posture: the audit trail asserts something false. The rule is also applied in four places (bash planner, Python telemetry, Python transport, TypeScript planner) with two different definitions (fallback chains considered in one, ignored in another).
**Required Fix:** Define "local" as a property the provider can be checked for: an HTTP provider (not `*-headless`, not `kind: cli`) whose declared endpoint host passes the validator's `check_insecure_optin` host acceptance (loopback, RFC1918 or `localhost`). Refuse `dispatch_group: local` at load (`endpoint_policy.validate_providers`) on any provider that fails it, apply the same rule in `hop_locality_of`, `_transport_policy` (and check the request host at request time), `hop-locality.py` and `isLocalVoice` (including `fallback_chain`, as the Python classifier already does), and add one test per surface with a hosted-endpoint provider labelled `local`. Keep one implementation where the languages allow (cheval + MODELINV + loader share `endpoint_policy`; the bash and TS planners mirror its host rule).
**Reference:** CWE-693 (Protection Mechanism Failure); CWE-807 (Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision); OWASP A05:2021 Security Misconfiguration.

### 2. Security — the trusted configuration never reaches the process that sends the prompt

- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/SKILL.md:117` — on a PR-head checkout Bridgebuilder reads providers/locality/exit from the base branch, but each voice is dispatched by cheval, which loads the checkout's `.loa.config.yaml`; a head that keeps a trusted provider's `keyless`/opt-in flags but changes its `endpoint`, `aliases` or `secret_env_allowlist` is admitted and the prompt (and a `{env:VAR}` credential) go where the head says.
**File:** `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/SKILL.md:117-118` (the claim); `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:602-605` and `:678-700` (`loadTrustedConfig` reads the head only for keyless/insecure declarations the trusted source lacks); `head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/core/multi-model-pipeline.ts:220-235` (the voice is created with no key and handed to the cheval delegate).
**Issue:** `headOnlyRefused` compares only two booleans per provider (`keylessOnlyInHead`, `insecureOnlyInHead`). A PR head that leaves `local-vllm: {keyless: true, allow_insecure_endpoint: "127.0.0.1"}` identical to the base but rewrites `endpoint` to `https://attacker.example/v1` (an operator-declared https endpoint skips the host allowlist in `validate_declared_endpoint`, `endpoint-validator.py:1289-1296`), or re-points `hounfour.aliases.<voice>` at a different provider, passes every check here; cheval then loads the checkout config and dispatches the review prompt there. For a trusted provider with `auth: "{env:X}"`, the Bearer credential travels with it. The pre-existing SKILL.md text records this invocation model as "no PR-head checkout" (`:116-117`); the sentence this PR adds (`:117-118`) asserts protection in exactly that case.
**Why This Matters:** The feature's stated purpose (D-7.5) is that an attacker-controlled head cannot declare its way to a credential or an insecure hop. The control is placed in Bridgebuilder's planner while the dispatch path reads a different file; the documentation now promises more than the code holds. Confidence is medium because the shipped scheduled invocation (`dispatcher.sh --repo`) runs in local mode on a trusted checkout; the exposure is the PR-event/`--pr` path the PR documents.
**Required Fix:** Either (a) on a pull request compute drift between the head's and the trusted view's `hounfour.providers`, `hounfour.aliases`, `hounfour.locality` and the secret allowlists and refuse the multi-model run on any difference with a distinct exit code, or (b) hand the trusted configuration to cheval explicitly (a config path cheval loads instead of the checkout's) so the dispatch reads what Bridgebuilder trusted. Correct SKILL.md to state exactly what is protected. Add a test where the head changes only `endpoint` of a trusted keyless provider.
**Reference:** CWE-693 (Protection Mechanism Failure); CWE-829 (Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere); OWASP A08:2021 Software and Data Integrity Failures.

## Observations

### 1. Callers — an exit 3 with nothing to show for it becomes success

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/skills/scheduled-cycle-template/contracts/session-cap-bb/dispatcher.sh:78` — `rc == 3` is recorded as `degraded: true` and converted to `exit 0` (`:89-90`) without checking that `bb-stdout.json` holds a run JSON; an exit 3 from any other source (a shell error inside `entry.sh`, a wrapper, a mixed-version `dist/`) is reported as a completed review.

content.text:
Review of sprint-1 (PR sprint-257) is complete. Verdict: **CHANGES_REQUIRED**. The feedback is at `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/engineer-feedback.md`, ends with the LOA-VERDICT trailer, and `verdict-derive.sh` reports it consistent with no violations. A one-line-per-finding copy is at `review.md` as the task brief asked.

**Two findings block the merge:**

- **Locality is a label, not a property.** Under `hounfour.locality: local_voices`, any model or provider marked `dispatch_group: local` is treated as local with no check of its endpoint host. I reproduced this with the head's own classifier: a declared provider pointing at `https://api.together.xyz/v1` classifies as local. The dissent added that a provider-block label is honoured by the planners but ignored by cheval's transport and MODELINV, so a planned-local hop runs without the request-time rules and is recorded as hosted.
- **Bridgebuilder's trusted config never reaches cheval.** The new SKILL.md text says providers, locality and exit follow the base branch even on a PR-head checkout, but every voice dispatches through cheval, which reads the checkout's config. A head that changes only a trusted provider's endpoint or an alias is admitted, and the prompt plus any `{env:VAR}` credential go where the head says.

The implementation report is the PR title alone, with no AC walkthrough or self-check record, which the skill treats as an automatic CHANGES_REQUIRED on its own.

**Fourteen observations, none counted.** The notable ones: the scheduled dispatcher converts any exit 3 to success without checking a run JSON exists; the health probe still applies its host allowlist to configured https providers, so the Azure example is refused; the config example's `budget_cents` comment contradicts the new summed estimate; `trust_env=False` under httpx also drops the operator's CA bundle; and the CHANGELOG the README links is not in this PR.

**Dissent.** The cross-model run completed with a clean envelope. The companion voice (claude-headless) produced one BLOCKING and six ADVISORY findings and no rejected payloads. I verified each against the PR head: four confirmed and folded in, three did not reproduce because the dissent read context from the workspace's newer framework copy.

**Skipped.** `br` is not installed, so no beads comment or label was recorded. `known-failures.md` is absent. The test suites could not be run here because the workspace holds only touched files; I read them instead and noted the missing cases.
